1.title: T&I Committee Republicans
1.description:
The Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure has jurisdiction over the nation's highways, bridges, railroads, transit and aviation systems, and maritime and waterborne transportation.  

The Committee also oversees programs for clean water infrastructure, pipeline safety, economic development, disaster preparedness and response, and the transportation of hazardous materials. 

These are issues that serve as the foundation of our economy and our way of life.  Committee Republicans are working to strengthen that foundation to ensure the safe, efficient transportation of people and goods, and provide the necessary infrastructure for our communities across the nation.

756.title: Press Conference: Unveiling of WRRDA (The Water Resources Reform & Development Act 2013)
756.description:
The leaders of the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Subcommittee on Water Resources and Environment introduced the Water Resources Reform and Development Act of 2013 (WRRDA) during a Wednesday press conference in the U.S. Capitol.

Through this type of water resources legislation, Congress authorizes the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to carry out its missions to develop, maintain, and support our Nation's vital port and waterways infrastructure needs, and support effective and targeted flood protection and environmental restoration needs.  Historically, Congress has passed such legislation every two years to provide clear direction to the Administration and the Corps, but no bill has been signed into law since 2007.  The Water Resources Reform and Development Act will be one of the most policy and reform focused measures of its kind in the last two decades.

864.title: Chairman Mica's Opening Remarks at Oct. 5 NextGen Hearing

Federal auditors, including the Inspector General of the Department of Transportation (DOT) and the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO), testified before Congress on Wednesday, October 5 to point to problems and rising costs in the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) critical NextGen air traffic control modernization effort.

FAA's poor management continues to delay NextGen progress, and the agency has failed to develop adequate benchmarks and a long-term plan for implementing the multi-billion dollar project to transition the nation's air traffic control system from ground-based radar and antiquated 1950s technology to a modern satellite-based system.

865.title: Rep. Petri at NextGen Hearing
865.description:
A Congressional hearing on Wednesday, October 5 examined the costs, benefits, progress and management of the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) NextGen air traffic control modernization program.

Wednesday's hearing, chaired by U.S. Rep. Tom Petri (R-WI), focused on the FAA's progress in delivering measureable benefits to aviation users, as well as the agency's projections for future benefits to be gained from federal and industry investment. The FAA has promised efficiency gains through NextGen by optimizing air traffic controller performance, consolidating obsolete facilities, enhanced safety improvements, and improved operational efficiency of the national airspace system. For example, the FAA estimates that with NextGen aviation users will save 1.4 billion gallons of fuel and see a 14 million ton reduction in carbon emissions through 2018. However, the airspace users who will be asked to invest in expensive NextGen compatible avionics must have confidence in FAA's ability to manage the program and deliver the benefits.

866.title: Rep. LoBiondo at Coast Guard Acquisitions Program Hearing
866.description:
The Subcommittee on Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation, chaired by U.S. Rep. Frank A. LoBiondo (R-NJ), held a hearing on Tuesday, October 4 to examine the Coast Guard Acquisition Program and the related challenges that have faced the Service since it took control of modernizing its aging fleet of assets in 2007.

The Coast Guard Acquisition Program has been experiencing significant cost overruns and setbacks that were the subject of a recent GAO report entitled "Action Needed as Approved Deepwater Program Remains Unachievable." The report found that it will be impossible for the Coast Guard to complete its major acquisitions without breaching its 2007 baseline of 20 to 25 years for construction and delivery at a total cost of $24.2 billion. The GAO estimates it could take an additional 10 years to complete and could cost at least an additional $5 billion.

This transportation system is also a key component of state and local economies and job creation efforts and is essential in maintaining economic competitiveness and national security.

The hearing focused on the EU's actions in the context of international law, and the impact of the EU's Emissions Trading Scheme on U.S. operators, the competitiveness of the U.S. aviation industry, and U.S. aviation jobs.

Beginning on January 1, 2012, all air carriers flying into or out of an EU airport will be forced to participate in the EU's Emissions Trading Scheme, despite objections by the United States and other governments. U.S. airlines have also challenged the policy before the European Court of Justice as a violation of international law.

Frank LoBiondo (R-NJ), on Wednesday examined the U.S. Coast Guard's current acquisitions programs (including continued acquisitions of assets associated with the former Deepwater program), and what improvements are necessary to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of the Service's acquisition of vessels, aircraft and other assets.

908.title: Rep. Shuster's Opening Statement at April 12 Railroads Subcommittee Hearing
908.description:
The Subcommittee on Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials, chaired by U.S. Rep. Bill Shuster (R-PA), conducted a hearing on Tuesday, April 12 to discuss reauthorization of federal hazardous materials transportation safety programs, as well as reforms to ensure safe, efficient hazmat transport and the reduction of regulatory burdens.

Some issues that were addressed at Tuesday's hearing were duplicative regulations and procedures, the issuance of special permits and approvals, the regulation of wetlines, and the opening of labeled and unlabeled packages.

909.title: Chairman Duncan's Opening Statement from Surface Transportation Bill Hearing
909.description: The Subcommittee on Highways and Transit, chaired by U.S. Rep. John J. Duncan, Jr. (R-TN), conducted a hearing on Tuesday, April 5, 2011 to receive testimony from Members of Congress on their proposals for improving and reforming transportation programs, cutting red tape and streamlining the project delivery process, increasing private sector participation in infrastructure financing, and wisely investing our limited infrastructure resources to create jobs through a surface transportation bill.

910.title: Chairman Denham's Opening Statement from Subcommittee Hearing on Consolidating Federal Buildings
910.description:
A Congressional hearing on Wednesday, March 6 explored the potential for establishing a process, based on the military's Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) Commission, for consolidating federal office space and improving real estate management to save taxpayers billions of dollars.
A civilian BRAC process, which would establish a fair process of evaluating federal space needs, has the potential to save the taxpayers billions of dollars by addressing the currently underutilized federal real property and over-reliance on costly leasing.

911.title: Petri on NMB Unionization Change
911.description: Aviation Subcommittee Chairman Tom Petri supporting FAA bill provision to restore union certification rules for aviation and rail workers.  The National Mediation Board (NMB) unilaterally changed the rules in 2010, despite 75 years of precedence, and despite such changes being properly the domain of Congress.

912.title: Mica on NMB Unionization Change
912.description: Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Chairman John Mica supporting FAA bill provision to restore union certification rules for aviation and rail workers.  The National Mediation Board (NMB) unilaterally changed the rules in 2010, despite 75 years of precedence, and despite such changes being properly the domain of Congress.

913.title: NMB Change: One-Way Democracy
913.description: Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Chairman John Mica calls the National Mediation Board's change to make the process for union certification easier, but not  the process for decertification, one-way democracy.

914.title: Petri Statement on FAA Bill
914.description: Aviation Subcommittee Chairman Tom Petri's statement on the House FAA bill (H.R. 658), a bill that will save taxpayers $4 billion in funding the nation's aviation programs.

915.title: Mica Statement on FAA Bill
915.description: Chairman John Mica's statement on the House FAA bill (H.R. 658), a bill that will save taxpayers $4 billion in funding the nation's aviation programs.

916.title: Mica Opposes Overregulation of Lithium Batteries
916.description: Committee Chairman Mica offered an amendment to FAA legislation that blocks enforcement of a pending, overly burdensome DOT regulation regarding the transport of lithium batteries.

917.title: Rep. Bob Gibbs (R-OH) During Floor Consideration of H.R. 872
917.description: The House approved H.R. 872, the "Reducing Regulatory Burdens Act of 2011," by a vote of 292 to 130. The bill was introduced by U.S. Rep. Bob Gibbs (R-OH), Chairman of the Water Resources and Environment Subcommittee. Transportation Committee Member and Chairman of the House Agriculture Committee's Subcommittee on Nutrition and Horticulture Jean Schmidt (R-OH) is a cosponsor of the legislation.

918.title: Rep. Jean Schmidt (R-OH) During House Floor Consideration of H.R. 872
918.description: The House approved H.R. 872, the "Reducing Regulatory Burdens Act of 2011," by a vote of 292 to 130. The bill was introduced by U.S. Rep. Bob Gibbs (R-OH), Chairman of the Water Resources and Environment Subcommittee. Transportation Committee Member and Chairman of the House Agriculture Committee's Subcommittee on Nutrition and Horticulture Jean Schmidt (R-OH) is a cosponsor of the legislation.

919.title: Chairman Mica Responds to Problem of Air-Traffic Controller Falling Asleep
919.description: In response to the Air-Traffic Controller falling asleep on the job at Reagan National Airport, Department of Transportation Secretary Ray LaHood proposed adding more staff to the control tower.  Chairman John Mica called this a "typical bureaucratic response," saying that additional staff will not remedy the problem.

920.title: Chairman John Mica Responds to Air-Traffic Controller Falling Asleep on Job
920.description: Following the March 2011 Reagan National Airport incident where two commercial jet liners landed without clearance because an air-traffic controller fell asleep on the job, DOT Secretary Ray LaHood proposed adding staff to control towers overnight.  Chairman John Mica called this a "typical bureaucratic response" because Reagan National Airport only averages two flight landings per day during the late night and early morning hours.

921.title: Mica Questions TSA Officials at House Oversight Committee Hearing
921.description: Congressman Mica attended a March 16 hearing held by the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and questioned TSA Officials on the invasive nature of their screening program and the inadequacy of their screening equipment.

922.title: Mica Questions TSA on Private Screening
922.description: The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform held a hearing on Wednesday, March 16 during which Congressman Mica questioned TSA officials on their screening equipment and its recently reported failure rates.

923.title: Mica Discusses SunRail at Maitland Field Hearing
923.description: House Transportation Committee Chairman John L. Mica (R-FL) conducted a Congressional field hearing on Monday, March 14 in Central Florida on pending major transportation legislation. The Committee is conducting an extensive series of meetings across the country with state and local officials and transportation stakeholders in order to gather information and innovative ideas for drafting a long-term reauthorization of the nation's highway, transit, and highway safety programs.

924.title: Subcommittee Chairman Jeff Denham's Opening Statement during GSA Hearing
924.description:
Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee Chairman Jeff Denham (R-CA) led a congressional hearing on cutting waste in the management of federal property on March 10, 2011.
The hearing focused on the General Services Administration's (GSA) Capital Investment and Leasing Program.

925.title: Mica on TSA 'Cooking the Books'
925.description: The Screening Partnership Program was established in the Aviation Transportation Security Act (ATSA) after September 11, 2001, to enable airport authorities to "opt-out" of all-federal screening and instead use private screening contractors under federal standards, supervision and oversight.  Previously, TSA has misleadingly claimed that the cost of the privatized screening program is at least 17 percent higher than the cost of using screeners who are TSA employees.

926.title: Chairman John L. Mica Discusses the Miami Intermodal Center on CBS
926.description: The MIC is one of the most advanced intermodal transportation facilities in the world and can serve as a model for similar projects throughout Florida and the United States.  U.S. Rep. John L. Mica (R-FL), the Chairman of the U.S. House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, hosted transportation officials from other Florida cities on a tour of the Miami Intermodal Center (MIC).  The tour took place on Friday, March 4, 2011.

927.title: Mica on Surface Transportation Extension
927.description: Chairman John Mica's opening statement during House floor consideration on March 2, 2011 of H.R. 662, the Surface Transportation Extension Act of 2011.

928.title: Gibbs on EPA Regulations
928.description: Water Resources and Environment Subcommittee Chairman Bob Gibbs (R-OH) statement from March 2, 2011 hearing to review the FY 2012 budget and priorities of the Environmental Protection Agency and its impacts on jobs, liberty, and the economy.

929.title: LoBiondo: Agencies Must Find Cost Efficiencies
929.description: Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee Chairman Frank LoBiondo (R-NJ) statement from March 1, 2011 hearing to review the Administration's budget requests for the U.S. Coast Guard, the Federal Maritime Commission, and the Maritime Administration.

930.title: Committee Visits Jonesboro, Asks for Input
930.description:
On February 24th, House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Members traveled to Jonesboro, AR for a listening session. The purpose of the public forum was to gather input from local officials and transportation stakeholders as Congress develops a long-term, job-creating reauthorization of the nation's highway, transit, and highway safety programs. 

KAIT covered the story.

933.description:
On February 22nd, House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Members traveled to Fresno, CA on a nationwide series of hearings and listening sessions. 936.description: On February 14th, House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Members traveled to West Virginia to launch a nationwide series of hearings and listening sessions. 949.description: Statement of U.S. Rep. Tom Petri (R-WI), Aviation Subcommittee Ranking Member, from September 16, 2010 hearing on the Federal Aviation Administration's Notice of Proposed Rulemaking on Airline Pilot Flight and Duty Time restrictions.

950.title: Mica on Obama Tax & Spend Proposal
950.description: Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Ranking Member John Mica (R-FL) on FOX and Friends (Sept. 16, 2010) to discuss President Obama's latest tax and spend, so-called stimulus effort which throws more money at our economic problems without addressing the problems with the first stimulus.  Much of the infrastructure funding in the first stimulus still has not been spent, and Mica supports cutting red tape for projects and getting the existing authorized funding out the door more quickly.

951.title: Rep. Candice Miller on Enbridge Spill
951.description: Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Member Candice Miller (R-MI) statement from September 15, 2010 hearing on the Enbridge pipeline oil spill in Marshall, Michigan.

953.title: Mica & LaHood Declare Gas Tax Hike Dead
953.description: U.S. Rep. John L. Mica (R-FL), the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Republican leader, declared a federal gas tax increase dead during a July 27, 2010 hearing on the stimulus. U.S. Secretary of Transportation Ray LaHood agreed that the Administration does not support any increase in the gas tax.

954.title: Duncan on Bridge Programs

955.description: Statement of U.S. Rep. Frank LoBiondo (R-NJ), Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee Ranking Member, from a July 20, 2010 hearing on the state of the United States' merchant fleet in foreign commerce.

956.title: Boozman on Stimulus Waste & Water Infrastructure
956.description: U.S. Rep. John Boozman (R-AR), Water Resources and Environment Subcommittee Ranking Member statement from a July 15, 2010 hearing on creating jobs through wastewater infrastructure investment.  Boozman states that too much of the so-called stimulus has been allocated to frivolous spending and not enough dedicated to infrastructure investment, such as clean water infrastructure.

957.title: Schock on Stimulus Waste
957.description: Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Member Aaron Schock (R-IL) speaks in favor of eliminating wasteful spending of millions in stimulus funds on signs to tell Americans that their stimulus dollars are being spent.  Schock sponsored the proposal as part of Republicans' YouCut initiative.

958.title: Shuster on Stimulus Waste
958.description: Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Member Bill Shuster (R-PA) speaks in favor of eliminating wasteful spending of millions in stimulus funds on signs to tell Americans that their stimulus dollars are being spent.

959.title: LoBiondo on Vessel Capacity
959.description: Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee Ranking Member Frank LoBiondo (R-NJ) statement from June 30, 2010 hearing on the Federal Maritime Commission's examination of vessel capacity to meet U.S. import and export demands.

960.title: Duncan on Red Light Cameras
960.description: Highways and Transit Subcommittee Ranking Member John J. Duncan, Jr. (R-TN) statement from a June 30, 2010 hearing on the utilization and impacts of automated traffic enforcement, specifically red light and speed cameras.

961.title: Petri on 14th FAA Extension
961.description: U.S. Rep. Tom Petri (R-WI), Aviation Subcommittee Ranking Member, on the regrettable but necessary passage of the 14th short-term extension of Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) programs.  The House approved the extension on June 29, 2010.  The House and Senate continue to struggle to reach agreement on a long-term reauthorization.

962.title: Shuster on Pipeline Safety
962.description: Statement of U.S. Rep. Bill Shuster (R-PA), Railroads, Pipelines and Hazardous Materials Subcommittee Ranking Member, from a June 29, 2010 hearing on hazardous liquid pipelines and how pipelines are regulated.

963.title: Diaz-Balart on GSA Waste
963.description: Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Ranking Member Mario Diaz-Balart (R-FL) statement from a June 17, 2010 hearing on the General Services Administration's (GSA) fiscal year 2011 Capital Improvement and Leasing Program.  Diaz-Balart highlighted the waste of taxpayer dollars represented by the Administration's proposal for funding federal construction and leasing projects for 2011. One proposed project would renovate an over-built and over-budget courthouse that currently allows 1,500 square feet of building space for each employee -- more space than many families occupy.

964.title: Petri on Proposed United-Continental Merger
964.description: U.S. Rep. Tom Petri (R-WI), Aviation Subcommittee Ranking Member, statement from a June 16, 2010 hearing on the proposed merger of United Airlines and Continental Airlines and its potential effects on consumers and the industry.

965.title: Duncan on FMCSA
965.description: U.S. Rep. John J. Duncan, Jr. (R-TN), Highways and Transit Subcommittee Ranking Member, statement from a June 23, 2010 hearing on the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration's new system of motor carrier oversight -- the Comprehensive Safety Analysis 2010 or CSA 2010.

966.title: LoBiondo on Oil Spill
966.description: U.S. Rep. Frank LoBiondo (R-NJ), the Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee Ranking Member, statement from a Congressional hearing on the Gulf oil spill, oil spill liability and financial responsibilities.

967.title: Mica on Oil Spill Legislation
967.description: U.S. Rep. John L. Mica (R-FL), the Republican leader of the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, speaks in support of emergency legislation to ensure that funds remain available to the Coast Guard to respond to the Gulf oil spill.

969.description: Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Ranking Member John Mica speaks with FOX NEWS regarding a federal report highlighting the failures of the Transportation Security Administration's behavior detection program (called SPOT).

970.title: Brian Rainville Testifies on Wasteful Stimulus
970.description: Brian Rainville, a teacher whose family farm is in Morses Line, Vermont, testifies that the federal government is planning to take a part of the farm and use millions in stimulus funds to rebuild a small border station at the Canadian border.  According to Mr. Rainville, the loss of the land would threaten the ability of his family to maintain the farm and put it out of business.

971.title: Diaz-Balart on Wasteful Stimulus
971.description: U.S. Rep. Mario Diaz-Balart (R-FL), the Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee Ranking Member, asks witnesses at a stimulus oversight hearing if the federal government should be wasting millions of dollars in stimulus funds to build a new eight-lane border facility at a crossing that sees 40 cars per day.  The stimulus project also threatens to drive a Vermont family farm out of business.

972.title: Diaz-Balart on Waste in Courthouse Program
972.description:
U.S. Rep. Mario Diaz-Balart (R-FL), Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee Ranking Member, calls the more than $800 million in tax dollars wasted on unnecessary courthouse construction an appalling example of government waste and mismanagement.

A Subcommittee hearing received testimony from the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO), which is working to finalize a report on the multibillion-dollar courthouse construction initiative of the federal judiciary and the General Services Administration (GSA).

973.title: Duncan on Clean Truck Programs
973.description:
Statement of U.S. Rep. John J. Duncan, Jr. (R-TN), Ranking Member of the Highways and Transit Subcommittee, from a hearing on implementation and impacts of the clean truck programs at the Port of Los Angeles and the Port of Long Beach.

Republicans applauded the progress made by the ports in dramatically cutting air pollution from trucks operating at their ports, and cautioned that efforts to reregulate the trucking industry and threaten small businesses are unnecessary for the success of clean truck programs.

974.title: Diaz-Balart on Economic Development Commissions
974.description:
At a Congressional hearing on the proposed fiscal year 2011 budgets for regional economic development commissions, Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee Ranking Member Mario Diaz-Balart (R-FL) stressed the importance of effectively leveraging commission funding and ensuring that job creation is a priority for distressed areas of the country.

Included among these commissions are the Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC), the Denali Commission, the Delta Regional Authority (DRA), the Northern Great Plains Regional Authority, the Southeast Crescent Regional Commission, the Southwest Border Regional Commission, and the Northern Border Regional Commission.

975.title: LoBiondo on Coast Guard Diversity

976.description: U.S. Rep. 977.title: Petri on NextGen
977.description: Statement of U.S. Rep. Tom Petri (R-WI), Subcommittee on Aviation Ranking Member, during a hearing entitled NextGen: Long Range Planning and Interagency Cooperation focusing on the nations continuing efforts to develop the next generation of air traffic control.

357.title: Clean Water Act of 2023 - Press Conference
357.description: Ranking Member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure Rick Larsen (D-WA), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Water Resources and Environment Grace Napolitano (D-CA), Rep. Don Beyer, Rep. Melanie Stansbury and over a hundred House Democrats will introduce the Clean Water Act of 2023. This legislation undoes the damage from the Supreme Court Sackett decision by reinstating the historic and bipartisan, federal-state partnership that has protected our rivers, streams, and wetlands for over 50 years; establishing a clear, level playing field for businesses and industries to thrive while protecting our precious natural resources; and ensuring clean water for our families and future generations.

622.title: "The Evolving Cybersecurity Landscape: Federal Perspectives on Securing the Nation's Infrastructure"
622.description:
Cyberattacks are a serious and evolving risk that affect transportation and infrastructure matters across T&I’s jurisdiction. Cyberattacks can result in tremendous financial damage, destruction of infrastructure assets, and even death. They impact governments, businesses, and individuals alike and have been growing in number and sophistication.
 
This hearing is the second of two full committee hearings on cybersecurity of the nation’s infrastructure. The first hearing was held in November 2021 and featured testimony from industry stakeholders and cybersecurity experts.
